title: Faithful flatness of henselization to base completion
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $I\subset A$ an ideal, and $\eta:A\to H$ the colimit of the full category of etale $A$-algebras $B$ with bijective canonical $A/I\to B/IB$ [lem-weil-pbc-pair-henselization]. Put $J=IH$. Suppose $\theta:\widehat A_I\xrightarrow{\sim}\widehat H_J$ is a ring isomorphism of adic completions [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] such that, for every $n\geq0$, $x\in\widehat A_I$ and $a\in A$, $x_n=a\bmod I^n$ implies $(\theta x)_n=\eta(a)\bmod J^n$. Then the map $\gamma:H\to\widehat A_I$ given by the completion map followed by $\theta^{-1}$ is faithfully flat [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map].

mathlib_searches.query: For a Noetherian pair the map from its henselization to its adic completion is faithfully flat
faithful flatness of the completion map from the henselization of a Noetherian pair

proof.text: Write $A^h=H$ and $I^h=J$. *Set-up.* By [lem-weil-pbc-pair-henselization], $A^h=\varinjlim_{B\in\mathcal C}B$, where $\mathcal C$ is the (essentially small, filtered) category of ring maps $A\to B$ with $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ etale and $A/I\xrightarrow{\sim}B/IB$, with coprojections $\iota_B:B\to A^h$ ($\eta=\iota_A$), $I^h=IA^h$, the pair $(A^h,I^h)$ is henselian, and $A/I\to A^h/I^h$ is an isomorphism. Since $I^h$ is generated by $\eta(I)$, $(I^h)^n$ is generated by $\eta(I^n)$, i.e. $(I^h)^n=I^nA^h$, for all $n\ge1$. The properties of the colimit supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-pair-henselization] hold for the specified cocone too: the unique isomorphism between two colimit cocones in the under category commutes with the structure map, carries its extended ideal to $J$, and transports the henselian property and the quotient isomorphism.

proof.text: *Each $B\in\mathcal C$ is Noetherian.* Let $B$ be an object of $\mathcal C$. As $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale, it is locally of finite presentation [def-weil-etale-morphism], so, applied to the affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $\operatorname{Spec}A$, the ring map $A\to B$ is of finite presentation [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation], in particular $B\cong A[x_1,\dots,x_n]/\mathfrak a$ is of finite type over $A$. Since $A$ is Noetherian, $B$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian].

source.place: Lemma Tag 0AGV, proof (the application of Algebra Lemma 00MB to $B$ needs $B$ Noetherian; left implicit in Stacks): Algebra Lemma Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence); Morphisms Lemma Tag 01TQ

proof.text: *For each $B\in\mathcal C$, $B^\wedge\cong A^\wedge\cong(A^h)^\wedge$.* Let $B\in\mathcal C$ and $B^\wedge=\varprojlim_nB/I^nB$ its $IB$-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] ($(IB)^n=I^nB$). $A\to B$ is flat [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat] and $A/I\to B/IB$ is an isomorphism, so $\beta_n:A/I^n\to B/I^nB$ is an isomorphism for every $n\ge1$ [lem-weil-pbc-flat-iso-mod-ideal-powers]; as in step 2 the $\beta_n$ induce an isomorphism $\varprojlim\beta_n:A^\wedge\xrightarrow{\sim}B^\wedge$. Let $\kappa_B:B^\wedge\to(A^h)^\wedge$ be the map induced by $\iota_B$ (levelwise $\bar\iota_{B,n}:B/I^nB\to A^h/I^nA^h$). Since $\iota_B$ is an $A$-algebra map, $\bar\iota_{B,n}\circ\beta_n=\eta_n$ (the assumed coordinate compatibility for $\theta$), so $\kappa_B\circ\varprojlim\beta_n=\theta$; as $\theta$ and $\varprojlim\beta_n$ are isomorphisms, so is $\kappa_B$. The inverse-limit comparison itself is [lem-weil-pbc-henselization-completion-data] applied to $A\to B$. The specified coordinate condition on $\theta$ identifies its coordinate map with $\eta_n$, since every quotient class has a representative in $A$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0AGV, proof: 'For each such $A\to B$ the induced map $A^\wedge\to B^\wedge$ is an isomorphism (see proof of Lemma 0AGU)'; the isomorphisms $A/I^n\to B/I^nB$: proof of Lemma Tag 0AGU (line 3105), via Algebra Lemma Tag 051H

proof.text: *$A^h\to(A^h)^\wedge$ is flat, hence $\gamma$ is flat.* Let $c:A^h\to(A^h)^\wedge$ be the completion map. For $B\in\mathcal C$ the composite $c\circ\iota_B:B\to(A^h)^\wedge$ equals $\kappa_B\circ c_B$, with $c_B:B\to B^\wedge$ the completion map (both are levelwise $b\mapsto\iota_B(b)\bmod I^nA^h$). $B$ is Noetherian (step 2), so $c_B$ is flat [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-completion-flat]; $\kappa_B$ is an isomorphism (step 3), so $c\circ\iota_B$ is flat (an isomorphism of $B$-algebras identifies the two module structures). Since $\mathcal C$ is filtered and $A^h=\varinjlim_{\mathcal C}B$ with coprojections $\iota_B$ (step 1), $c$ is flat [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-rings-flat]. As $\theta^{-1}$ is a ring isomorphism, $\gamma=\theta^{-1}\circ c$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].

source.place: Lemma Tag 0AGV, proof: 'By Algebra, Lemma 00MB (lemma-completion-flat) the ring map $B\to A^\wedge=B^\wedge=(A^h)^\wedge$ is flat for each $B$. Thus $A^h\to A^\wedge=(A^h)^\wedge$ is flat by Algebra, Lemma 05UU (lemma-colimit-rings-flat)'

proof.text: The henselian factorization criterion [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-factorization-criterion] gives $J\subseteq\operatorname{Jac}(H)$. Let $q:H/J\xrightarrow{\sim}A/I$ be the inverse of the quotient isomorphism from [lem-weil-pbc-pair-henselization], and let $\pi:\widehat A_I\to A/I$ be coordinate evaluation at 1, surjective because a representative in $A$ gives a completion element. The condition on $\theta$ identifies its first-coordinate map with the inverse of $q$. Evaluating $\theta\gamma(h)=c_H(h)$ therefore gives $\pi\gamma(h)=q(h\bmod J)$. For a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\subset H$, $J\subseteq\mathfrak m$; its quotient is a proper ideal of $H/J$, and its image under $q$ is proper. The extension $\mathfrak m\widehat A_I$ maps into this proper ideal under $\pi$, hence is proper. Flatness from the previous step and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-faithfully-flat-maximal-ideals] prove faithful flatness. No description of the kernel of $\pi$ is required.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0AGV, proof: 'Since $I^h=IA^h$ is contained in the Jacobson radical of $A^h$ and since $A^h\to A^\wedge$ induces an isomorphism $A^h/I^h\to A/I$ we see that $A^h\to A^\wedge$ is faithfully flat by Algebra, Lemma 00HP (lemma-ff)'
